claims: All eighteen types have a registry contract with a render, payload, completion, error-surface and ARIA contract; the completed types (Q02, Q04, Q10, Q11, Q12, Q13, Q15) have grading bindings.

One instance of each of the eighteen types is answered through the component and integration API in a scripted session; every answer goes through session.dispatch("answer", …), and the answer map round-trips through serialize()/deserialize() unchanged.
The capture-grading parity table shows all eighteen stored payloads consumed by their frozen engines with no adapter: the audit finds zero adapters and zero value rewrites.
The Q03 template response runs the manual-rubric pending path: pending, never fake-scored.
The navigator map cells carry the completion verdict from SimInputsRegistry.completion: the eighteen answered slots are complete and the seven deliberately incomplete cases are not.
The review warning list names exactly the incomplete slots with their Latvian missing names and carries role="alert" for the screen-reader announcement.
A whitespace-only Q15 is BLANK_RESPONSE with zero points and every criterion denied; a non-blank Q15 is pending with no verdict and no machine points.
Errors never destroy raw input: the stored payload is the string the learner typed, and an error is an annotation on the completion verdict.
evidence: evidence/N22_COMPONENTS_RECORD.json (N22-B: pointer/keyboard payload parity and the mid-interaction abort)

claims: The three in-file smoke vectors (numeric, classification, ordering) are registered, assert the eighteen-type island, drive SimSession and pass.
The session machine remains the only writer: the integration offers no setter, the accessors hand out deep copies, and one answer() call is exactly one dispatch.

The label bank is term-keyed: no string literal in src/inputs/*.ts carries a standalone unit symbol, every dotted ARIA key resolves in data/terms.json, the rendered names match the resolved terms, and the input.* terms carry no English UI vocabulary.

notes: The compiled input modules are strict TypeScript output and are committed; the drift guard (tools/compile_n21_ts.py --check) keeps them in step with src/inputs/*.ts.
The three smoke vectors are appended to src/smoke-subset.js and are inlined, so they consume runtime-JS headroom. Their appended size is measured against the N21 ledger figure for the same file.

The projection above is what the merge build will measure: the island is inlined, the modules are not. A positive projected_artifact_overrun_bytes means the enforced artifact-total ceiling is exceeded by that many bytes once the island lands; AGENTS.md sets the budget on the measured requirement, so the resolution is a visible re-budget (coordinator / N31), not a silent shrink of the contract.

not_claimed: No official examination, grade or proctoring status.
No screen-reader acceptance: the ARIA evidence is a mechanical structural check (roles, names, key resolution); N33 performs the live pass.
No browser-render acceptance: the render descriptions are JSON, not pixels.
No semantic grading of free text: Q15/Q16 stay pending and Q03 stays manual-rubric.
No claim that the four variants are four finished questions.
No keyboard-vs-pointer acceptance here: that fixture belongs to N22-B; this record references its output rather than duplicating it.
